translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs again joined in slandering him, to every extreme.

sentences.zh: 後主問諸太姬，憫默不對，及三問，乃下床拜曰：「老婢合死，本見和士開道孝徵多才博學，言為善人，故舉之。

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign questioned Tai Ji; she grieved in silence and would not answer; after three questions she left the couch and bowed, saying, "This old serving-woman deserves death. I saw He Shikai say that Xiaozheng was broadly learned and talented and called him a good man, and so I recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Sovereign questioned Tai Ji. She grieved in silence until he asked a third time; then she left the couch and bowed. "This old serving-woman deserves death," she said. "He Shikai told me Xiaozheng was learned and gifted and a good man, and so I raised him up.

sentences.zh: 比來看之，極是罪過，人實難知。

translations.literal: Watching him lately, he is nothing but guilt — men are hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Watching him now, he is nothing but guilt — men are hard to know.

sentences.zh: 老婢合死。

translations.literal: This old serving-woman deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: This old serving-woman deserves death.

sentences.zh: 」後主令韓長鸞檢案，得其詐出勑受賜十餘事，以前與其重誓不殺，遂解珽侍中、僕射，出為北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: " The Later Sovereign ordered Han Changluan to investigate the case; more than ten matters were found in which he had forged edicts to receive gifts; because of an earlier heavy oath not to kill him, Ting was relieved of attendant-in-ordinary and vice director, and sent out as governor of Northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The Later Sovereign ordered Han Changluan to investigate. They found more than ten cases of forged edicts and illicit gifts. Because of an earlier solemn oath not to kill him, Ting was stripped of attendant-in-ordinary and vice director and sent out as governor of Northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 珽求見後主，韓長鸞積嫌於珽，遣人推出栢閣。

translations.literal: Ting asked to see the Later Sovereign; Han Changluan, who had long resented Ting, sent men to push him out of the Cypress Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Ting begged an audience with the Later Sovereign. Han Changluan, who had long hated him, sent men to thrust him from the Cypress Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 珽固求面見，坐不肯行。

translations.literal: Ting insisted on a face-to-face audience and sat, refusing to move.
translations.idiomatic: Ting insisted on seeing him face to face and sat, refusing to budge.

sentences.zh: 長鸞乃令軍士牽曳而出，立珽於朝堂，大加誚責。

translations.literal: Changluan then ordered soldiers to drag him out, set Ting in the court hall, and reviled him severely.
translations.idiomatic: Changluan ordered soldiers to drag him out, set him in the court hall, and reviled him without mercy.

sentences.zh: 上道後，令追還，解其開府儀同、郡公，直為刺史。

translations.literal: After he had set out on the road, an order recalled him, stripped his open office and state equal to the Three Excellencies and his commandery dukehood, and left him a plain governor.
translations.idiomatic: After he had set out, an order recalled him, stripped his open office, state equal to the Three Excellencies, and commandery dukedom, and left him a plain governor.

sentences.zh: 至州，會有陳寇，百姓多反。

translations.literal: On reaching the province, Chen raiders appeared and many of the people rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his province, Chen raiders struck and much of the populace rose against him.

sentences.zh: 珽不關城門，守埤者皆令下城靜坐，街巷禁斷行人，雞犬不聽鳴吠。

translations.literal: Ting did not close the city gates; he ordered the men on the ramparts to leave the walls and sit in silence; streets were barred to travelers; chickens and dogs were forbidden to cry.
translations.idiomatic: Ting did not shut the gates. He ordered the rampart guards down to sit in silence, barred the streets to foot traffic, and forbade chickens and dogs to make a sound.

sentences.zh: 賊無所聞見，不測所以，疑惑人走城空，不設警備。

translations.literal: The bandits heard and saw nothing, could not fathom the reason, grew doubtful as men fled and the city stood empty, and set no watch.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits heard and saw nothing, could not guess his design, took fright as men fled and the city seemed empty, and posted no watch.

sentences.zh: 珽忽然令大叫，鼓噪聒天，賊大驚，登時走散。

translations.literal: Ting suddenly ordered a great shout; drums and clamor shook heaven; the bandits were greatly alarmed and at once scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Ting suddenly ordered a great shout; drums and clamor shook the sky; the bandits panicked and scattered at once.

sentences.zh: 後復結陣向城，珽乘馬自出，令錄事參軍王君植率兵馬，仍親臨戰。

translations.literal: Later they again formed ranks and advanced on the city; Ting rode out himself, ordered recorder Wang Junzhi to lead horse and foot, and still personally went into the fight.
translations.idiomatic: Later they formed ranks and marched on the city again. Ting rode out himself, ordered recorder Wang Junzhi to lead horse and foot, and still fought in the front line.

sentences.zh: 賊先聞其盲，謂為不能拒抗，忽見親在戎行，彎弧縱鏑，相與驚怪，畏之而罷。

translations.literal: The bandits had earlier heard he was blind and thought he could not resist; suddenly they saw him in person on the field, bending the bow and loosing arrows; they were alarmed together, feared him, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits had heard he was blind and thought him helpless; then they saw him in the battle line, bending the bow and loosing shafts. They stared in shock, feared him, and broke off.

sentences.zh: 時穆提婆憾之不已，欲令城陷沒賊，雖知危急，不遣救援。

translations.literal: At the time Mu Tipo still hated him without end and wished the city to fall to the bandits; though he knew the danger was acute, he sent no rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Tipo still hated him without end and wished the city would fall to the bandits. Though he knew the peril was acute, he sent no rescue.

sentences.zh: 珽且戰且守十餘日，賊竟奔走，城卒保全。

translations.literal: Ting fought and held for more than ten days; the bandits at last fled; the city was preserved in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Ting fought and held for more than ten days. The bandits at last fled, and the city stood.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子君信，涉獵書史，多諸雜藝。

translations.literal: His son Junxin ranged widely in books and histories and mastered many miscellaneous arts.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junxin ranged widely in books and histories and mastered many miscellaneous arts.

sentences.zh: 位兼通直散騎常侍、聘陳使副、中書郎。

translations.literal: He held the concurrent posts of regular attendant of the unimpeded staff, deputy envoy on the mission to Chen, and langzhong in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He held concurrent posts as regular attendant of the unimpeded staff, deputy envoy on the mission to Chen, and secretariat langzhong.

sentences.zh: 珽出，亦見廢免。

translations.literal: When Ting went out, Junxin was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting fell, Junxin was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 君信弟君彥，容貌短小，言辭澀訥，少有才學。

translations.literal: Junxin's younger brother Junyan was short in stature and halting in speech, with little talent or learning.
translations.idiomatic: Junxin's younger brother Junyan was short in stature, halting in speech, and slight in talent.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，位至東平郡書佐。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he rose to clerk of Dongping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's Daye era he rose to clerk of Dongping commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡陷翟讓，因為李密所得，密甚禮之，署為記室，軍書羽檄皆成其手。

translations.literal: When the commandery fell to Zhai Rang, he was taken by Li Mi, who treated him with great courtesy and appointed him recorder; military documents and urgent dispatches were all written by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery fell to Zhai Rang, Li Mi took him, treated him with great courtesy, and made him recorder; military documents and urgent dispatches all passed through his hand.

sentences.zh: 及密敗，為王世充所殺。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, he was killed by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was defeated, Wang Shichong killed him.

sentences.zh: 珽弟孝隱，有文學，早知名。

translations.literal: Ting's younger brother Xiaoyin had literary talent and was known early.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's younger brother Xiaoyin had literary gifts and was known early.

sentences.zh: 詞章雖不逮兄，亦機警有辯，兼解音律。

translations.literal: Though his compositions did not match his elder brother's, he was also quick-witted and eloquent, and understood music.
translations.idiomatic: His compositions did not match his brother's, yet he was quick-witted and eloquent and understood music.

sentences.zh: 魏末為散騎常侍、迎梁使。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he was regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and received the Liang envoy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei he was regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and received the Liang envoy.

sentences.zh: 時徐君房、庾信來聘，名譽甚高，魏朝聞而重之，接對者多取一時之秀，盧元景之徒並降階攝職，更遞司賓。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Junfang and Yu Xin came on embassy; their fame was very high; the Wei court, hearing of it, held them in weight; those who met them mostly took the outstanding men of the day — men such as Lu Yuanjing all stepped down a rank to assist in office, taking turns as masters of reception.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Junfang and Yu Xin came on embassy then, men of towering fame. The Wei court, hearing of them, treated the occasion with gravity and chose the day's finest to meet them — Lu Yuanjing and others all stepped down a rank to assist, taking turns as masters of reception.

sentences.zh: 孝隱少處其中，物議稱美。

translations.literal: Xiaoyin, young among them, won praise in public discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyin, still young among them, won praise in public discussion.

sentences.zh: 孝隱從父弟茂，頗有辭情，然好酒性率，不為時重。

translations.literal: Xiaoyin's younger cousin Mao had considerable gift for words, but loved wine and was frank by nature, and was not held in weight by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyin's cousin Mao had a gift for words but loved wine and was blunt by nature, and the age did not esteem him.

sentences.zh: 大寧中，以經學為本鄉所薦，除給事，以疾辭，仍不復仕。

translations.literal: In the Daning era he was recommended by his native district for classical learning, made gentleman attendant, declined on grounds of illness, and never again took office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daning era his native district recommended him for classical learning; he was made gentleman attendant, declined on grounds of illness, and never served again.

sentences.zh: 珽受任寄，故令呼茂，茂不獲已，暫來就之。

translations.literal: When Ting received a weighty commission, he therefore had Mao summoned; Mao could not refuse and came for a time to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting received a weighty commission he summoned Mao; Mao could not refuse and came for a time.

sentences.zh: 珽欲為奏官，茂乃逃去。

translations.literal: Ting wished to memorialize and give him an office; Mao then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Ting meant to memorialize and give him an office; Mao fled.

sentences.zh: 珽族弟崇儒，涉學有辭藻，少以幹局知名。

translations.literal: Ting's clansman younger brother Chongru was versed in learning and had literary polish; in youth he was known for practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's clansman Chongru was versed in learning and had literary polish; in youth he was known for practical ability.

sentences.zh: 武平末，司州別駕、通直常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was vice governor of Si Province and regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was vice governor of Si Province and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 入周，為容昌郡太守。

translations.literal: On entering Zhou he was governor of Rongchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou took the realm he was governor of Rongchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，終宕州長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui he ended as chief administrator of Dang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he ended as chief administrator of Dang Province.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
